requirement:
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject, any contributed source, or an acknowledgment supplied
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs` MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.

When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs`.

**Initial mandatory inputs: definitions referenced by the subject, contributed sources and acknowledgments.**
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors]` covers terms reached from the subject's own text. The subject cites `terms.unit`, and `terms.unit` and `terms.value` reference each other. The test asserts that exactly two definition inputs are supplied. That shows the transitive closure is complete, has no duplicates, and terminates on the cycle.
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[mandatory_git_inputs_require_staging_declarations_sources_and_terms]` covers terms referenced from a contributed source. A staged source with a `{term}` reference makes `terms.ready` a mandatory definition input. An unstaged term file is reported as an error.
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[acknowledgment_only_terms_are_supplied_and_validated_without_implementation_reads]` covers terms referenced only from an acknowledgment body. The `{term}` reference is to `terms.boundary`, which depends on `terms.unit`. The test asserts that both definitions' text reaches the prompt. It also asserts that the implementation body is absent and that no outline input is created. The definitions are recorded, and evidence validation then detects a changed transitive definition and a missing definition input.

**Declaration completeness, including the phrase option.**
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_introduced_by_a_read_are_supplied_and_recorded_before_submission]` asserts that each definition input's text starts with `:::{definition}` followed by a `:phrase: ` line.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms]` asserts the full definition text. It checks that `text[1]` equals `:phrase: value`.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[declaration_text_reaches_the_model_redacted]` asserts the exact full declaration text of `terms.value`. It also asserts that the definitions supplied for a requirement read, `terms.base` and `terms.value`, are transitive and duplicate-free.

**Terminology dependencies introduced by an additional source read.**
- The test in `src/authoring/mod.rs` has the model read `fn[work]`, which references `terms.value`, a term in a cycle with `terms.unit`. It asserts that the recorded definitions are exactly `["terms.unit", "terms.value"]`, once each. It asserts that the second request, which is the one before submission, delivers "A unit of" text, and that the first request did not contain it.
- `reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms` and `src/authoring/pages.rs#mod[tests]/fn[paged_inputs_carry_their_definitions_and_deliver_only_their_own_inputs]` verify that line-range reads, item reads and paged reads carry and record their definitions.

No obligation is left without a test and assertion. The implementation was not needed to reach this conclusion.

text: :::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject, any contributed source, or an acknowledgment supplied
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs` MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`.
:::{req} fixme_inputs
For a requirement or example assessment, the initial request MUST include every
valid named `{fixme}` reference to the subject found under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except a reference inside one of
the subject's sites under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, in this
form:
```text
Acknowledgment {
file: String,
item: String,
body: String,
issues: Array<{ reference: String, state: "open" | "closed" }>,
`file` and `item` MUST locate the containing source by project-relative path and
outline selector, using `<root>` for a whole file. `body` MUST contain the
reference's complete fenced commentary without its fences or source-comment
delimiters, including its option lines, redacted under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`. `issues` MUST give every distinct issue
its `:github:` lines name, in their order, with state supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.github_reads`. Acknowledgments MUST be ordered by
file and position in the file and MUST carry no line numbers or containing
implementation source.
The locations and bodies MUST be protected against staleness by the reference-set
digest under {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`; the acknowledgment MUST NOT
create an outline input merely to cover its containing source. Actual reads of
that source MUST still be recorded under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`. Sources MUST satisfy
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`; an inaccessible acknowledgment
MUST be reported before inference.
Terminology definitions referenced by an acknowledgment's body MUST contribute
their complete, transitive declarations to the mandatory input set under
{cite}`requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs` and MUST be recorded as
definition inputs. Only the acknowledgment's body MUST contribute these
dependencies; its containing implementation source MUST NOT be supplied merely
to discover them.
